skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: The skill generally matches its pet-video analysis purpose, but it silently creates or reuses identity state, stores service tokens locally, and sends media and identity data to remote services with limited user-facing control.

dimensions.detail: Reading a user-selected local video and uploading it is expected for server-side analysis, but the skill also reads workspace identity state, creates a workspace data directory/database, and contacts fixed external lifeemergence.com services without a strong privacy notice.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, startup service, scheduled task, or remote code retrieval was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, though one requirements entry appears malformed as yaml==6.0.3.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md discloses server APIs, history lookup, and automatic identity handling, but it instructs automatic cloud queries and hidden identity use without a clear consent boundary, retention explanation, or authorization model for history retrieval.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The code creates or reuses a shared SQLite database under the workspace data directory and stores user records plus token/open_token values across runs; this is persistent credential-adjacent state beyond simple one-off analysis.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Remote pet video analysis and cloud history lookup are purpose-aligned and disclosed, but the package also includes automatic external login/registration, local identity and token persistence, and broad generic HTTP/CRUD helpers that exceed a narrowly scoped video-analysis skill.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only with media you are comfortable uploading to the provider, and avoid using it in shared workspaces unless you accept that it may create persistent local identity records and store service tokens. The publisher should add an explicit privacy notice, retention/deletion details, and a scoped authentication model before this is treated as low-risk.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Partly supported. The manifest does disclose server-side APIs, cloud history, and automatic identity handling, so the skill is not purely misleading; however, local identity-file use, SQLite token persistence, auto-registration/login, and broad HTTP helpers are under-disclosed enough to support Review.
[YR4] expected: Downgraded. The visible match appears tied to Unicode/emoji content in bilingual metadata rather than hidden instructions or parser-confusing payloads; no concealed override text was found in SKILL.md.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Supported in part. History report lookup is documented, but reusable default-user creation and broad local user-account persistence are more durable and account-like than the pet-analysis purpose requires.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Supported. The code reads workspace identity state, silently registers/logs in against a health-service endpoint, and stores token/open_token values in the local sys_user table without clear user-facing disclosure.
[LP3] unexpected: Supported as a scoping concern. The skill relies on shell execution of Python, local file reads/writes, SQLite persistence, and outbound network calls but does not define a tight permission boundary or allowlist in metadata.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote media submission is expected for server-side video analysis, but the artifacts do not clearly explain data retention, deletion, exact remote services, or local persistence behavior before upload/query operations.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded. The skill is bilingual at the manifest level and mostly Chinese in runtime messages; this is usability/locale friction rather than a material security issue.
[P9] expected: Downgraded. The whitespace finding corresponds to formatting alignment in Python code, and inspection found no hidden prompt instructions around it.
[E1] unexpected: Supported. The auto-login path sends openId/mobile/source-style identity fields to an external health endpoint as an implicit side effect of requests, which is not clearly necessary or disclosed for pet video analysis.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded. The subprocess-related docstring is stale because the execution code is commented out and nonfunctional; it is confusing documentation but not active persistence or execution behavior.
